highlights.title: Card authorization off the monolith, with zero downtime
highlights.hook: Moved the busiest path in the company to a new service while it handled 2M payments a day.
highlights.problem: Card authorization lived in a 9-year-old Rails monolith. p99 was 900ms, every deploy was a risk, and the payment network was threatening penalties for slow responses.
highlights.did: I proposed a strangler plan: a Go service fed by shadow traffic, compared response by response against the monolith for six weeks, then moved over 1% of merchants at a time with an instant switch back. I led four engineers through it and wrote the comparison tooling myself.
highlights.outcome: p99 fell from 900ms to 120ms. No authorization failed during the cutover, and the old code path was deleted four months after we started.

highlights.title: 1,400 tests to a new framework in 3 weeks, with an agent
highlights.hook: A migration the team had postponed for two years, done with Claude Code and a coverage diff.
highlights.problem: The platform's tests ran on a framework that was no longer maintained. Rewriting them by hand was estimated at four months, so it never made a roadmap.
highlights.did: I split the suite into batches of about 50 tests, had Claude Code rewrite each batch, and wrote a script that compared coverage and test names before and after. Two engineers reviewed every diff; anything that touched card data was rewritten by hand.
highlights.outcome: Done in 3 weeks instead of an estimated 4 months. Coverage went from 81% to 83%, and CI got 40% faster.

highlights.title: Ledgerline: a double-entry library, built twice
highlights.hook: Written by hand in 2017, paused for six years, and revived with AI in 2025.
highlights.problem: Every payments codebase I had seen kept money in mutable balance columns, and none of them could explain a balance to an auditor.
highlights.did: I wrote an open-source double-entry library in Ruby with immutable entries and idempotent posting. In 2025 I picked it up again with AI: a Go port, a reconciliation CLI and full documentation.
highlights.outcome: Used in production at two companies, 1,900 stars, and the Go port reached feature parity in five weeks of evenings.
